subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Agent Collaboration Enhancement: Capability Profiling + Shared Blackboard + Layered Memory + Token Cost Governance

question: Should #35203 remain a broad core roadmap umbrella for generic multi-agent seams, be split into narrower canonical issues, or move mostly to plugins/ClawHub with only missing core APIs tracked here?
rationale: The RFC spans core/plugin ownership, persistent SQLite state, memory visibility, security boundaries, provider-cost admission, and config/API surfaces, so automation cannot choose the permanent product boundary safely.

options.title: Split into narrow core seam decisions
options.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella and route concrete work to scoped issues for budget admission, meeting/coordination primitives, memory visibility, and capability-routing APIs before implementation.

options.title: Plugin/ClawHub-first
options.body: Treat the collaboration stack as external orchestration unless a specific missing plugin or SDK API blocks it.

options.title: Keep as a monolithic core RFC
options.body: Accept the broad stack as a future core feature, knowing it will require a large architecture, security, storage, and upgrade design before any PR.

recommendation.title: Split into narrow core seam decisions
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella and route concrete work to scoped issues for budget admission, meeting/coordination primitives, memory visibility, and capability-routing APIs before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest observed connection to product-direction decisions for adjacent multi-agent and heavy-orchestration scope discussions.
